en: 14 miles upstream, a lake sat|behind a wall of packed earth.
Cut it open, and you see the problem:
60 feet of water, held back by dirt.
At about 3:10 p.m.,|the dam gave way.
20 million tons of water|poured down the valley,
a wave 35 feet high at its crest.
At the Stone Bridge, the wreckage|piled 40 feet high, and caught fire.
